clue.text: Almost perfect clothes for leisure activity (7)

indicators.note: almost the whole word: its last letter is dropped

blocks.note: PURE without its final E
a suit of clothes

explanation.surface: Someone's leisurewear is nearly flawless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clothes for leisure' reads as one phrase about casual wear; the break falls after 'clothes', and 'leisure activity' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a hobby followed in spare time is called a pursuit, as in outdoor pursuits.

clue.text: One on the beach said not to be alone (6)

definitions.text: One on the beach said not to be alone

blocks.note: the surface suggests a person sunbathing; the setter means a stone lying on the shore
a nod to the saying 'you're not the only one on the beach', used to deflate someone who thinks they are unique

explanation.surface: A lonely beachgoer is reassured they have company.
explanation.walkthrough: The full saying is 'you're not the only pebble on the beach', said to someone who thinks they are the only one who matters.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom itself names the stone: there are always other pebbles on a beach.

clue.text: Faulty effect of snapping night flight (3,3)

blocks.note: the camera flash bouncing off the retina so pupils glow in a photo
an overnight plane journey that leaves passengers bleary

explanation.surface: A photographer complains about a flaw in their night-time pictures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Snapping' looks like breaking or biting; it is taking photographs.
explanation.definitionFit: Both the photographic flaw and the overnight flight share one name because both leave eyes looking bloodshot.

clue.text: Diagnostic aid extremely reliable (10)

blocks.note: ultra = extremely, as in ultra-cautious
sound = reliable, as in sound advice

explanation.surface: A medical test is praised as very dependable.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a review of a test's accuracy, so 'extremely reliable' looks like praise rather than two pieces laid end to end.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by function: an ultrasound scan lets doctors see inside the body to diagnose.

clue.text: Dragged – why to the church? (5)

blocks.note: the reason for going somewhere is given with 'to'
the purpose of a trip to church in the surface: marrying

explanation.surface: A reluctant groom asks why he was hauled off to the church.
explanation.walkthrough: The question answers itself: why go to the church? To wed. Run together, that reply spells the definition's synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a car that is towed is dragged behind another.

clue.text: Still retaining ultimate method of payment (7)

indicators.note: to retain is to hold inside

blocks.note: a still is a photograph, a pic
ultimate = last

explanation.surface: A payment method is still being kept on as the final option.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Still' looks like an adverb meaning 'yet'; it is the noun, a single frame from a film.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang: credit and debit cards are made of plastic, so paying by card is paying with plastic.

clue.text: Prudish Olive re-read author, a Holocaust survivor (5,4)

indicators.note: reading the letters again in a new order rearranges them

blocks.note: prim = prudish
OLIVE rearranged

explanation.surface: A prudish woman called Olive rereads a Holocaust memoir.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Olive' looks like a woman's name; only its five letters matter.
explanation.definitionFit: Primo Levi, an Italian chemist, survived Auschwitz and wrote If This Is a Man about it.

clue.text: The last word in service (4)

blocks.note: the idiom means the very best of its kind; the setter means literally the final word spoken
the surface suggests waiters or customer care; the setter means a church service

explanation.surface: Someone boasts of offering the very best service.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'last word' literally and 'service' as worship, and the clue describes what is said at the close of a prayer.
explanation.definitionFit: Amen closes prayers, hymns and services, so it is literally the last word said.

clue.text: Adding together twelve 0s and a 1 makes a huge number (8)

definitions.text: Adding together twelve 0s and a 1 makes a huge number

blocks.note: the surface suggests arithmetic, which would total 1; the setter means placing the digits side by side, a 1 then twelve zeros
the result of writing those digits together

explanation.surface: An arithmetic lesson on building a huge number out of digits.
explanation.walkthrough: Summing twelve zeros and a one gives only 1, which is the trap; writing them in a row gives ten to the twelfth power.
explanation.definitionFit: In modern usage the name for ten to the power twelve is this number.

clue.text: Big bags carrying lettuce for tsar’s cavalry (8)

indicators.note: in a down clue the bags carry the lettuce on top of them, so it comes first

blocks.note: cos is a variety of lettuce, called romaine in America
sacks are big bags

explanation.surface: Big sacks of lettuce are hauled along as supplies for the tsar's horsemen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carrying' tempts a container, but putting the lettuce inside the bags fails; here the bags hold it up, as the column is read downward.
explanation.definitionFit: Cossack horsemen from the southern steppes served the Russian tsars as cavalry.

clue.text: Old president finally gets changed, going to basin (5)

indicators.note: the final letter of the name is swapped for another

blocks.note: Joe Biden, former US president
his last letter N is replaced

explanation.surface: A former president gets a makeover and heads to the bathroom.
explanation.walkthrough: Nothing in the clue supplies the new letter; the definition and crossers settle it.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by kind: the low bathroom fixture for washing is a type of basin.

clue.text: Perhaps tactful remarks describing snow that has settled (5,4)

blocks.note: small untruths told to spare someone's feelings; 'perhaps' because not every one is tactful
read as a sentence: when snow has settled, something pale rests on the ground

explanation.surface: Tactful words spoken about a landscape covered in settled snow.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half turns the phrase into subject and verb, which is why it reads as a description rather than a definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A harmless fib is a white lie, and the same two words describe settled snow.

clue.text: Bless attack (3,5,2)

blocks.note: a priest's gesture of blessing or healing, touching someone's head
to seize or assault someone physically

explanation.walkthrough: The two meanings are opposites, one gentle and one violent, which is the charm of the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The same phrase covers a priest's blessing and a physical assault.

clue.text: Paul Nash guarding part of his arm (4)

indicators.note: the name holds the answer inside it

blocks.note: four letters straddling the gap between first name and surname

explanation.surface: The painter Paul Nash protects his arm.
explanation.walkthrough: Paul Nash was a British war artist, but his name matters only for what it hides: pa(ULNA)sh.
explanation.definitionFit: Anatomy: the forearm has two bones, the radius and the ulna.

clue.text: Jogs round area and sells leftovers (10)

indicators.note: to go round something is to surround it, so the jogs enclose the area

blocks.note: jogs to the memory are reminders
a = area

explanation.surface: A runner jogs around the neighbourhood and sells off leftover stock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jogs' looks like running; it is the noun, prompts to the memory.
explanation.definitionFit: Trade jargon: a publisher remainders unsold copies by selling them off cheaply.

clue.text: Jargon from mouth was spouting: I approve (12)

blocks.note: gob is British slang for mouth
blood was spouting: it bled
ego is Latin for I
to OK something is to approve it

explanation.surface: Someone spouting jargon finishes with a satisfied 'I approve'.
explanation.walkthrough: The colon makes 'I approve' look like a quotation; it is two more pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Near synonym: gobbledegook is incomprehensible official or technical language.

clue.text: Method of communication depressed canine (9)

blocks.note: feeling blue = depressed
a canine is a pointed tooth

explanation.surface: A sad dog is being used to send messages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Canine' pairs with 'depressed' to suggest a gloomy dog; it is the tooth.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by function: the wireless standard lets phones and headsets talk to each other.

clue.text: One clamped on wrist perhaps to keep close behind guard (8)

blocks.note: a wristwatch
to dog someone is to follow closely

explanation.surface: A handcuffed prisoner is shadowed by a guard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clamped on wrist' suggests handcuffs; it is a timepiece.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally a dog kept to guard property, and figuratively a body that guards the public interest.

clue.text: Distinctive feature of a piece of land one has (8)

definitions.text: a piece of land one has

blocks.note: a characteristic quality, as in the properties of a metal

blocks.clueFragment: a piece of land one has
blocks.note: real estate that belongs to someone

explanation.surface: Describing what makes a patch of land special.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Of' looks like it ties the feature to the land; it only joins the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: One word covers both a quality something possesses and land someone possesses.

clue.text: Concerned with flying a Lear, caution must be exercised (12)

indicators.note: the letters are put through their paces, moved about

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 12 letters

explanation.surface: Advice to pilots of a Learjet: take care.
explanation.walkthrough: A Lear is a Learjet, a small private plane, which keeps the surface in the air.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: aeronautical describes the science and practice of flight.

clue.text: Petition Lord’s, for example (6)

blocks.note: a formal request, as to a court or to God
the one beginning 'Our Father' is the best-known example

explanation.surface: A petition is sent to Lord's, the London cricket ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lord's' looks like the famous cricket ground; it is the first word of a Christian prayer's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A request to God or a court, and the second definition is by example.

clue.text: Stick notice in this place (6)

blocks.note: an ad is a notice
here = in this place

explanation.surface: An instruction to put up a notice right here.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stick' reads as an order to pin up the notice; it is the definition, a verb meaning cling.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: glue makes things adhere, or stick, to a surface.

clue.text: Text for printer is not original (4)

definitions.note: 'is not original' describes what a copy is

blocks.note: newspaper jargon for written material ready to be typeset
what a duplicate is, as opposed to the original

explanation.surface: A printer's text turns out not to be original.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is a description rather than a synonym: whatever is not the original is a duplicate.
explanation.definitionFit: Journalists call text for printing copy, and a duplicate is a copy.

clue.text: Daring last desperate stand here for Soviets (10)

indicators.note: in a frantic state, the letters thrown into disorder

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 10 letters

explanation.surface: A daring last-ditch stand by the Soviets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Last desperate stand' reads as one phrase; 'desperate' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The Soviet city on the Volga held out against the German siege of 1942-43, a turning point of the war.

clue.text: Sportsman removing top in bed (5)

indicators.note: in a down clue the top is the first letter

blocks.note: a player is a sportsman

explanation.surface: An athlete takes his shirt off in bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bed' looks like where the sportsman is; it is the definition, as in a bed of rock.
explanation.definitionFit: Geology: a bed of rock or sediment is one stratum in a stack.

clue.text: Dossier of wasted life (4)

indicators.note: ruined, so the letters are wrecked

blocks.note: anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A dossier records someone's wasted life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wasted life' reads as a sad phrase; 'wasted' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a dossier is a collection of papers on one subject, kept in a folder.

clue.text: Such a sleepy town? (9)

blocks.note: the surface means dull and quiet; the setter means used for sleeping
asks for the word that goes before 'town' in the phrase

explanation.surface: A question about a quiet, sleepy town.
explanation.walkthrough: A dormitory town is one where commuters only sleep, working elsewhere; the question mark flags the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: From the Latin for sleep, a commuter town is one where people only come home to bed.

clue.text: Sports car of energy and character (1-4)

blocks.note: E = energy in physics
a type is a printed character

explanation.surface: A sports car full of energy and personality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Character' suggests personality; it is a printed letter, a piece of type.
explanation.definitionFit: Named example: the Jaguar E-Type of the 1960s is a classic British sports car.

clue.text: Why gent fancied Welsh girl (7)

indicators.note: fancy as an adjective: elaborated, rearranged

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 7 letters

explanation.surface: Someone wonders why a gentleman took a shine to a Welsh girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancied' reads as 'was attracted to'; it signals an anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a traditional Welsh girl's name, from Gwynedd.

clue.text: Substitute that offers protection for game (7)

blocks.note: a player kept on the bench to come on as a replacement
a protected area where wild animals are kept safe

explanation.surface: A substitute player offers cover in a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Game' looks like a sports match beside 'substitute'; it means wild animals.
explanation.definitionFit: A replacement player, and in 'game reserve' the land that shelters wildlife.
